This is more than a building; it's a fully integrated live/work property designed for those who value both functionality and creative expression. Combining architectural scale and modern adaptability, it offers a rare opportunity to own a space that supports a dynamic, multi-purpose lifestyle. Originally a Lucky Strike warehouse and later, among other uses, home to the avant-garde Capp Street Project and the last 20 years an art studio, this property carries a legacy of innovation and cultural relevance. Its industrial origins remain evident, while thoughtful transformations have created a flexible environment designed by Stanley Saitowitz. At the center is a dramatic 50-by-60-foot main hall with 24-foot ceilings and a skylit pitched roof, and a suspended sculptural spiral iron staircase leads from the ground floor to a rooftop deck, providing open-air space for gatherings or a quiet haven. Two additional ensuite rooms and a flexible space with a green wall for workouts or collaborators. Also, a laundry room and an additional staircase leading down to the main level. A wide garage fits 2 cars with 2 EV charging stations and ample storage ensures functionality. Adaptable and distinctive, this property is suited for residential living, creative production, business use, or a hybrid of all three, an increasingly rare offering that supports both lifestyle and work in one cohesive environment. This is a home for innovation, invention, and imagination.

In excellent condition, this turnkey property offers versatility for continued SRO operation or potential reconfiguration, making it a standout choice for investors seeking strong returns in a high demand market.

Situated on the 4th floor at 719 Valencia Street, this bright and peaceful end unit offers an appealing blend of natural light, modern design, and exceptional urban convenience. Facing a quiet alley rather than bustling Valencia, the home enjoys a notably quiet setting while remaining close to some of the city's best dining, culture, and transit options. The open-concept living, dining, and kitchen area is lined with oversized windows that flood the space with indirect natural light throughout the day, creating an airy and welcoming atmosphere. The layout centers around a great room, starting with the kitchen: quartz countertops, Bosch dishwasher, Smeg Stove, Liebherr refrigerator, and a spacious pantry with wire rack shelves. There is a generous walk-in closet in the living room. The wide-plank engineered wood flooring lends a clean, contemporary aesthetic. The enormous bedroom feels especially bright and inviting, with windows on opposite walls that enhance both the light and sense of openness. The bathroom offers a contemporary, minimalist aesthetic: rustic tile floor, floating vanity, and subway tile shower surround. The Miele washer and dryer are in a closet off the hall just outside of the bathroom. The building elevates city living, quite literally, with its sprawling rooftop deck with multiple lounge areas, two BBQ stations, and panoramic views of the Mission District. Additional highlights include assigned bike parking, a secure storage unit, and professional management. FirstService Residential keeps the building exceptionally well maintained. With a 99 Walk Score, 100 Transit Score, and 92 Bike Score, this central location places acclaimed taquerias, vibrant nightlife, cultural attractions, and transit options just outside your door. Whether you're a first-time buyer, pied--terre seeker, or investor, this is a compelling opportunity to own a bright, quiet, and beautifully designed residence in one of San Francisco's most vibrant neighborhoods.

First home, pied-a-terre, or rental property. A smart entry into San Francisco real estate for a first-time buyer, a perfectly positioned city base for a second home, or the right rental investment for an investor building a portfolio. Low price point and low HOA dues make this one of the better value plays in the heart of the Mission District. A one-bedroom in a 1909 Victorian building, converted to condominiums in 2008, that blends classic architecture with a modern interior. High ceilings, warm wood floors, and a private terrace that most SF condos at this price point simply don't have. The terrace sets this one apart. A sprawling private terrace that runs the entire width of the condo, with a brick backdrop that sets the vibe. Dinner outside, cocktails before heading out, or just fresh air when you need it. Private outdoor space like this in the Mission at this price is rare. Inside, the open living, dining, and kitchen flows together. The kitchen is anchored by quartz counters, a gas range, and a generous breakfast bar that works for morning coffee, a laptop during the day, or friends gathered in the evening. The bedroom opens to the terrace and has a large closet that keeps storage simple and out of sight. The bathroom is finished with marble floors, a glass-enclosed shower, and a generous medicine cabinet. In-unit laundry and a large private storage closet just outside the front door round out the condo. Upstairs, the shared rooftop delivers panoramic views of the city and the vibrant Mission District. Between the private terrace and the rooftop, this condo is the natural gathering point. Available furnished if desired. Turnkey from day one. The building allows 30-day minimum rentals. Whether you're offsetting costs as a first-time buyer, leasing out between visits as a second home owner, or running it as an investment property, the flexibility is built in. Situated in the Mission District, with Dolores Park, Valencia Street nightlife, and vibrant taquerias all within easy reach. Restaurants, bars, and cafes right outside the door. Trader Joe's close by. MUNI, BART, and tech shuttles make commuting easy. Whether you're heading across the city or down the peninsula, this location makes it effortless. Walk Score 99, Transit Score 100, Bike Score 62.

1908. Two years after the earthquake and fire, San Francisco was an exciting place full of activity and westward expansion. In this year, the stunning row of homes that contains 789 Arguello was added to the grand 1st Avenue, renamed Arguello after Jos Daro Arguello, who served as a Spanish governor of Alta and Baja California in the early 1800s. A short walk from Lyon Street stairs and Fillmore Street boutiques, this was, as now, an elegant and central location. Refreshed and ready for life today, 789 Arguello looks out over the wide tree-lined sidewalks and its own tranquil rear garden. It has a spacious entry foyer, front living room with decorative bird's eye maple mantle and huge double-parlor style primary bedroom. Restored old growth Douglass fir floors draw you down the hall past the 2nd bedroom and revamped bath to the large eat-in kitchen. The kitchen was recently renovated with new cabinetry and appliances in on-trend shades of green, ivory, and gold. At the rear of the home, a sunny 3rd bedroom leads to the garden. Below this room, there is a dedicated storage, craft, or workout room with an adjacent garage area with up to 2 car parking (depending on car size) and laundry hookups for the exclusive use of this unit. This is the sanctuary that will become the hub of your social life as you meet with friends before and after long days in the park, where you lace up your shoes before relaxing evening strolls and enjoy many years of convenient city living. The neighborhood can't be beat. In addition to all of the historical attractions still available today, you can get most of what you need right across the street at the well-stocked Arguello Market, special occasion gifts at Iris & Emerson, and a burrito said to give you 50 miles worth of power at Velo Rouge. Venturing around the corner, more delights only found in SF - a secret sushi place in a converted garage (Tekka, but of these photos are of somewhere else it's so secret, call ahead and there is no website), Cinderella Bakery's famous Piroshki, shop for one-of-a-kind handmade ceramics at Yonder on Cabrillo or follow your feet down to Ariscault and all of the delights of Clement just a few blocks north.

This rare Rousseau-built Spanish Mediterranean home in the heart of the Mission District has remained in the same family for generations, preserving many of its original architectural details. Soaring vaulted ceilings with exposed beams, dramatic arched windows, intricate wrought iron detailing, original hardwood floors, vintage tile work, period fireplaces, and richly preserved character throughout. Even the original kitchen and bathroom tile work has survived—an increasingly rare find in San Francisco where so many homes of this era have been stripped or overly remodeled. The scale is exceptional, with approximately 2,460 square feet across two levels featuring a classic floor plan that includes a grand formal living room, formal dining room, eat-in kitchen with breakfast area, two bedrooms, and a bath on the main level, plus a substantial lower level with family room, wet bar, laundry, storage, and expansive garage space. The home sits in one of the Mission's most vibrant residential pockets near Dolores Park, Valencia Street, and the neighborhood's bustling taquerias and cafes. The next owner will likely undertake meaningful improvements and restoration work over time, but the architectural foundation here is incredibly special. Homes with this level of intact character, scale, and provenance rarely come to market anymore. This home offers a genuine opportunity to restore and steward an important piece of San Francisco residential architecture.

381 Lyon Street is a mixed-use investment ideally located in the prestigious Pacific Heights district, one of San Francisco's most desirable and supply-constrained submarkets. Situated steps from the Lyon Street stairs and a stone's throw from neighborhood icons such as Zuni Cafe and Blue Bottle Coffee, the property sits at the intersection of Fillmore Street and the Financial District, benefiting from strong pedestrian traffic, limited new supply, and enduring housing demand. The property consists of a 42-room Residential Hotel (SRO) above a large, street-level commercial space, providing diversified income from two complementary uses. The ground-floor commercial space is occupied by a long-standing neighborhood legacy business that has operated along the Lyon Street corridor for over 40 years. The tenant executed a new 10-year lease in late 2025, offering long-term income stability and approximately one-third reimbursement of property taxes, reducing operating expenses and enhancing cash-flow. The residential hotel has been owned and conservatively operated by the seller's family for nearly 50 years, spanning two generations. Pride of ownership is evident throughout, with extensive upgrades to lighting, flooring, and other interior improvements. Additional amenities include on-site coin-operated laundry for the residential hotel. The seller is offering the property with 17 vacant units, creating a compelling value-add opportunity for a new owner to implement updated marketing, improve occupancy, and drive future revenue growth. The building as a whole has benefited from substantial capital investment totaling over $400,000, including a completed seismic retrofit, upgraded fire alarm system with horns, full sprinkler coverage, and new double-paned energy-efficient windows throughout. A unique physical advantage is the building's accessibility from three sides, allowing for efficient maintenance, future renovations, and capital improvements. Conveniently located and backed by stabilized long-term commercial income from a legacy tenant, 381 Lyon Street represents a compelling opportunity to acquire a well-maintained mixed-use asset with built-in stability and upside. With existing residential vacancy, a new owner is positioned to control tenancy, shape the future of the property, and execute a long-term investment vision.

This home has been lovingly upgraded with luxury Duchateau Vernal Como hardwood flooring with cork underlayment, all new lighting including the dining chandelier Skygarden'' made by Flos (designed by Marcel Wanders), custom cabinetry, smart Hunter Douglas window coverings including a blackout shade for the primary bedroom suite. A smart home system is set up using Lutron, Philips Hue, Powerview by Hunter Douglas, Ecobee, August home, Eve, and more! The primary bedroom suite is spacious and features a spa-like bathroom and a large walk-in closet with custom cabinetry. The second bedroom is currently used as an office but would also make a great guest bedroom. You have an additional full bath, in-unit laundry, and central heat/AC. The kitchen features high-end appliances and plenty of counter space. In the living area, there is a custom bar area, as well as cabinets and a TV setup for relaxing. Enjoy time on your private patio, or go just a short distance to the 75-ft heated lap pool, spa, sauna, fitness studio, outdoor grill/lounge, billiards room, conference room, and private movie theater. The residence also features 24/7 concierge service. Additional features include central A/C, a storage cage, 1 car secure garage parking with two bike racks and a private EV charger. With easy access to Lyon Street stairs, Fillmore Street boutiques, and the manicured garden squares, you will love living in the stately period architecture of Pacific Heights.

Nestled in the prestigious Pacific Heights, this 12th floor, 2BR 2BA corner unit offers panoramic Bay views, sweeping vistas of the Fillmore Street boutiques, and the stately architecture of Lyon Street. This unique floor plan features wall-to-wall windows, luxurious finishes, and resort-like amenities. Interior highlights include Gaggenau appliances, Kohler fixtures, Vadara countertops, Porcelanosa tile, and Domus & Domus cabinetry. Enjoy a state-of-the-art fitness center, dry sauna, heated outdoor pool and spa, exhibition and catering kitchens, a library, business center, guest suite, and 24-hour lobby attendant. This unit is a modern retreat in one of San Francisco's most coveted addresses.
